doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
title: First New Orleans job: Rialto with Lawrence Toca
summary: Filling in for Sadie in 1929, Billie played with Lawrence Toca and Alphonse Picou at the Rialto before going back to Birmingham.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: I played in Mobile, with Slim Hunter, broadcast at Battle House in Mobile, at that radio station there, broadcast. Battle House there, with Slim Hunter out there, that's right. That was in Mobile. What did Slim play? Banjo. He was a great entertainer, great songs and a banjo. Well, what was the first band you played with when you came over here? The first band I came here when I played with? Lawrence Toka and I went to work with Alphonse Picou at the Rialto nightclub out on Jefferson Davis Parkway. Who else was in the band? Lawrence Picou, Johnny David, Ernest Milton and myself. Let's see. Trumpet, piano, granite, bandger, and drum. Five of us. There's five pieces.
Ernest Milton played what? Drummer. And Johnny Dave played what?
When you came over here to take Sadie's place, did you stay that time?
No, I just came there to wait for her until she got better from being sick.
That was in 29? Yeah. Was that?
It was 29. Then I went back to Birmingham. Back to my band in Birmingham, back to the Nighthawk office in Birmingham.
